newsitem.title: JAPAN: New firm planned to take over Nissan Life - paper.
newsitem.headline: New firm planned to take over Nissan Life - paper.

text.p: The Life Insurance Association of Japan plans to form a new company to take over the business of failed Nissan Mutual Life Insurance Co with help from other companies, including Nissan Motor Co Ltd and Hitachi Ltd, a Japanese business daily said on Tuesday.
Nihon Keizai Shimbun said in its Tuesday evening edition that the new company, expected to be formed in July, will make fresh contracts as well as take over Nissan Life's operations.
A spokesman for the industry group declined to confirm the report, adding that the group was still studying Nissan Life's financial condition.
The paper said the industry group will ask eight companies in the Nissan and Hitachi groups to invest a total of 50 billion yen in the new company.
The eight companies are Nissan, Hitachi, Nissan Fire & Marine Insurance Co Ltd, Nippon Suisan Kaisha Ltd, Japan Energy Corp, Hitachi Metals Ltd, Hitachi Cable Ltd and Nichirei Corp the paper said.
Other Japanese life insurers will contribute about 200 billion yen to the new company through the industry's policyholder protection fund, the paper said.
Insurers will also provide financial aid of 50 billion yen to the new company in the form or subordinated loans or equity participation, the paper said.
